content.text:
I reproduced the scoring from today's cached Artificial Analysis (AA) free-tier data (742 models, 61 of 144 provider models scored). Yes, the pricing formula needs to change, but the bigger problem is which AA row each model is scored against.

## What the data shows

**1. The cost term barely works above about $1 per task.** `1 / cost` is min-max normalized, so the one cheapest model (MiMo-V2.6-Flash, $0.13) sets the scale and the median model scores 0.04 out of 1 on cost.

| agenticCoding: halving the cost | Worth, in intelligence points |
|---|---|
| $10 → $5 | 0.13 |
| $2 → $1 | 0.67 |
| $0.40 → $0.20 | 3.4 |

Example: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (intelligence 54.5, $10.02 per task) and GPT-6.1 Sol (54.6, $1.27 per task) differ by 0.013 score from cost. An 8x price gap counts for about one intelligence point.

**2. Every model is scored at maximum reasoning effort.** The mapping uses AA's base slug, which is the "Max" variant. Effort changes cost and latency far more than the choice of model does:

| Claude Sonnet 5.5 variant | Intelligence | $ per task | End-to-end response time |
|---|---|---|---|
| Max (what is scored) | 54.5 | 10.02 | 457 s |
| Xhigh | 49.9 | 4.09 | 36 s |
| High | 41.5 | 1.64 | 16 s |

**3. Tokens per second is the wrong speed signal.** Claude Opus 5.5 Max streams 96 tokens/s but takes 686 s end to end; Gemini 4 Hydrogen takes 67 s. AA's free tier includes `median_end_to_end_response_time_seconds` for all 61 scored models. Speed has the same outlier problem as cost: one 420 tokens/s model sets the scale.

**4. The provider price adjustment almost never fires.** Provider prices equal AA's list prices for 58 of 61 models. So `outputToInputRatio` (including llmWiki's 0.2) only affects three rows, and the rankings are effectively AA's rankings filtered by each provider's lineup.

**5. Flat plans have a real price signal that is ignored.** OpenCode Go's per-model monthly cap ranges from $15 to $100 and is already parsed. On a $10 flat plan, the scarce thing is tasks per month under the cap, not dollars per token.

**6. There is no second quality signal to add.** AA's Engineering Index is on the free tier but correlates with the Intelligence Index at r = 0.995 for the scored models. Cache prices exist on both sides, but they would only matter for the same three rows as point 4, so I would not pursue them.

**7. The categories barely differ.** codeReview and agenticCoding return the same top two for all four providers. With a log-scaled cost, llmWiki and softwareFactory change their picks; agenticCoding changes only its second pick.

## Round 1

❓ **Q1 - Log-scale cost**: Should cost be scored on a log scale, so halving the cost is worth the same amount at any price point? In the simulation this keeps Gemini 4 Carbon top for agenticCoding on Copilot, but makes llmWiki pick GPT-6.1 Sol instead of Gemini 4 Carbon and Claude Opus 5.5.

➡️ Yes. It is the smallest change that makes the cost weight mean something, and it is fully static.

---

❓ **Q2 - Reasoning-effort variants**: Should each AA effort variant (Low to Max) be scored as its own candidate, with the best-scoring variant per model shown as, for example, "Claude Sonnet 5.5 (High)"? The alternatives are to keep Max only, or to pin one effort per provider by hand.

➡️ Yes. Effort is a setting developers control, and it is the largest price lever in the data. It also lets categories differ honestly: softwareFactory would pick lower efforts than codeReview.

---

❓ **Q3 - Keep a weighted sum**: Should the score stay a weighted sum rather than become "cheapest model above an intelligence floor per category"? The floor is closer to how a developer thinks, but it adds a hard cliff and a hand-picked threshold per category.

➡️ Yes, keep the weighted sum, with the weights restated as exchange rates (Q6).

---

❓ **Q4 - Speed from end-to-end time**: Should speed be measured by AA's end-to-end response time (log-scaled) instead of output tokens per second? It measures one short response, not a whole agentic task, but it does include thinking time.

➡️ Yes. Tokens per second rewards models that produce a lot of reasoning quickly and still keep you waiting.

---

❓ **Q5 - Plan caps for OpenCode Go**: Should OpenCode Go's cost metric become tasks per month under the model's cap (cap ÷ cost per task), while Copilot, OpenCode Zen and ClinePass stay on dollars per task? This works because rankings are already per provider. I have not checked whether ClinePass or Copilot publish comparable per-model caps.

➡️ Yes. A $60 cap against a $15 cap is a 4x difference in what the subscription actually buys.

---

❓ **Q6 - Drop normalization and the per-category ratio**: If Q1 is yes, should the config state exchange rates directly ("a halving of cost is worth N intelligence points, a halving of response time is worth M") instead of 0–1 weights over a min-max pool, and should `outputToInputRatio` be removed? Today a new cheap model on ClinePass shifts every Copilot score, and the ratio is cosmetic.

➡️ Yes to both. The numbers become readable and stable day to day, and the llmWiki ratio stops implying precision it does not have.
Q5: ignore them for now, rest as recommended

content.text:
Settled so far: log-scaled cost, effort variants as candidates, weighted sum, end-to-end response time for speed, exchange rates instead of normalized weights, `outputToInputRatio` removed, plan caps ignored.

I simulated that design on today's data, and it surfaced one problem that reopens part of Q1.

## What the simulation showed

- **Variants triple the pool.** 161 candidate rows instead of 61, from the same 61 provider models. 36 models have only one AA configuration; 15 have five or six.
- **Pure log cost has no bottom.** With variants, cost per task spans $0.005 to $11.82. GPT-6 Luna (Low), with intelligence 9.7 at $0.005 per task, ranked first for softwareFactory on OpenCode Go and third on Copilot. Ten doublings of cheapness outweigh any amount of intelligence.
- **A floor fixes it.** Treating anything under $0.25 per task as $0.25, and anything under 15 s as 15 s, removes that model from every top three.

The formula I simulated: score = intelligence − *a* × log2(cost per task) − *b* × log2(response time ÷ 60 s), so a model at $1 per task and 60 s scores exactly its intelligence.

Top pick per provider with the floor applied and the rates proposed in Q8:

| Category | Copilot | OpenCode Go | ClinePass |
|---|---|---|---|
| agenticCoding | Gemini 4 Carbon (Medium), $4.68, 36 s | Gemini 4 Argon (High), $9.95, 59 s | Kimi K3.1 Pro, $3.68, 88 s |
| codeReview | Gemini 4 Carbon (High), $5.48, 123 s | Gemini 4 Argon (High), $9.95, 59 s | Kimi K3.1 Pro, $3.68, 88 s |
| softwareFactory | GPT-6.1 Sol (Medium), $0.36, 16 s | Claude Haiku 5.5 (Xhigh), $0.25, 69 s | DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017, $0.30, 16 s |
| llmWiki | GPT-6.1 Sol (Medium), $0.36, 16 s | Claude Haiku 5.5 (Xhigh), $0.25, 69 s | DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017, $0.30, 16 s |

OpenCode Zen's top pick matches Copilot's in every category.

## Round 2

❓ **Q7 - "Cheap enough" floor**: Should cost below $0.25 per task and response time below 15 s earn no further credit? The alternative is a minimum intelligence per category, but provider lineups top out at very different levels (ClinePass at 46.5, Copilot at 60), so one absolute minimum would empty some lists.

➡️ Yes, with both floors as two global constants in the config.

---

❓ **Q8 - Exchange rates**: Should the categories use these rates, in intelligence points lost per doubling?

| Category | Per doubling of cost | Per doubling of response time |
|---|---|---|
| agenticCoding | 1.5 | 1 |
| codeReview | 1 | 0.5 |
| softwareFactory | 5 | 3 |
| llmWiki | 4 | 1 |

They are the current weights translated to the log scale and rounded. The softwareFactory rate means a model half the price may be 5 points less intelligent and still tie.

➡️ Yes as a starting point. They give the picks in the table above, which I think read sensibly.

---

❓ **Q9 - One row per model**: Should each model appear once per list, at its best-scoring effort, so the top two are two different models rather than, say, GPT-6.1 Sol at Medium and at High?

➡️ Yes. The shortlist is for choosing a model; the effort label is the setting to use with it.

---

❓ **Q10 - Assume every effort is selectable**: Should scoring assume each provider lets you pick any effort level AA has benchmarked? I have not verified this per provider or harness. The alternative is a hand-maintained allow-list per provider.

➡️ Yes, stated as a known simplification in the config notes. An allow-list is manual upkeep on data no source publishes.

---

❓ **Q11 - Keep the four categories and the price adjustment**: Should all four categories stay, with llmWiki now just a cost-heavy preset, and should the provider price adjustment stay as is (cheapest price row per model, fixed 3:1 output-to-input blend)? codeReview and agenticCoding now differ in the effort they recommend, which they did not before.

➡️ Yes. Neither is worth redesigning for the three models where provider prices differ from AA's.

---

❓ **Q12 - What the site shows**: Should the score be shown as "net intelligence points" (roughly 30 to 60 instead of 0 to 1), with columns for effort, intelligence, $ per task and response time, replacing tokens per second and blended $ per 1M tokens?

➡️ Yes. Every column would then be an input to the score a reader can check.

Q11: can you somehow capture with scores things like copywriting style, design, data ingest and aggregation? Just looking for opportunities here

input.recap: Artificial Analysis has no signal for copywriting or design, but its free tier has a usable one for data work. Its docs also say the response-time field we chose stops returning data on December 10, 2026. Nothing in the repo is changed; four decisions remain.

content.text:
Data ingest and aggregation can be scored from the free tier; copywriting and design cannot be scored from Artificial Analysis (AA) at any tier I could see. Checking the docs also turned up a deadline that breaks the response-time choice from Q4.

## What AA offers for those three

- **Copywriting and design:** nothing. The free tier has no writing or design score, and AA's arenas rate image, video and speech models, not LLM output. The reference page was cut off near the end (speech, music and measurements sections), so I did not read every endpoint.
- **Data ingest and aggregation:** the free tier already returns six Capability Indexes that the pipeline ignores. Two are relevant, and unlike the Engineering Index they carry signal that intelligence does not:

| Index | What AA says it covers | Correlation with intelligence | Typical gap from what intelligence predicts |
|---|---|---|---|
| Finance & Accounting | Spreadsheets, analysis, workflows across business apps; 15% non-hallucination | 0.966 | 3.7 points |
| Strategy & Ops | Operations and support workflows; 35% agentic tool use | 0.931 | 5.9 points |
| Engineering | Engineering knowledge, science, agentic coding | 0.995 | 1.5 points |

  A quarter of both relevant indexes is business knowledge recall, which is noise for a developer's data task.
- **Pro tier:** it adds individual benchmarks that would fit better, including non-hallucination rate, long-context reasoning, instruction following, office-deliverable Elo, context window and `time_per_task_seconds`. I did not look up what Pro costs.

## The deadline

AA's docs say every field in the `performance` block returns null from December 10, 2026. That block holds the end-to-end response time we picked in Q4, and its replacement `performance_v3` has no end-to-end field on the free tier.

- **A substitute exists:** time to first answer token + 500 ÷ output tokens per second, from `performance_v3`. That reproduces AA's definition; for Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Medium) the old block's numbers imply exactly 500 tokens.
- **The values shift:** `performance_v3` reports means, not medians. GLM-5.3-Flash goes from 43 s to about 100 s, and GPT-6.1 Sol (Xhigh) from 116 s to about 79 s.
- **Coverage is the same:** 120 of 129 indexed models have `performance_v3`, against 119 with the old field.

## Round 3

❓ **Q13 - Response time from `performance_v3`**: Should response time be computed as time to first answer token + 500 ÷ tokens per second from `performance_v3`, never reading the deprecated block?

➡️ Yes. Building on a field that goes null in 24 days would mean redoing this in December.

---

❓ **Q14 - A data category**: Should there be a fifth category, for example `dataAggregation`, scored on the Finance & Accounting index instead of the Intelligence Index, with cost and time rates like llmWiki's? The alternative is Strategy & Ops, which has more tool use and more independent signal, but no non-hallucination component.

➡️ Yes, on Finance & Accounting. Accuracy matters more than tool use when aggregating data, and its description names spreadsheets and analysis.

---

❓ **Q15 - Quality metric per category**: Should each category name its quality metric in the config (`qualityMetric: "intelligenceIndex"` by default), validated against the fields AA actually returns? Q14 needs this, and it lets a Pro field slot in later without a redesign.

➡️ Yes. llmWiki stays on intelligence for now; the Legal and Economics indexes are closer on long-context work but are 30% domain knowledge.

---

❓ **Q16 - Leave copywriting and design unscored, stay on the free tier**: Should we add no category for copywriting or design, and not design around Pro fields now? Scoring them would need either a second data source such as a public web-design arena, which I have not researched, or a paid AA key.

➡️ Yes. A category with no real signal behind it would just repeat the intelligence ranking under a misleading name.

content.text:
I read "those 3 scores" as the Engineering, Finance & Accounting and Strategy & Ops indexes, blended with intelligence into a per-category quality score, with `financeWork` replacing the `dataAggregation` idea. Say so if you meant something else.

## The proposal I simulated

Score = quality − *a* × log2(cost per task) − *b* × log2(response time ÷ 60 s), where quality is a weighted mix of the four indexes that sums to 1.

| Category | Intelligence | Engineering | Finance & Accounting | Strategy & Ops | Points per cost doubling | Points per time doubling |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| agenticCoding | 0.2 | 0.6 | – | 0.2 | 1.5 | 1 |
| codeReview | 0.3 | 0.7 | – | – | 1 | 0.5 |
| softwareFactory | – | 0.6 | – | 0.4 | 5 | 3 |
| llmWiki | 0.5 | – | 0.25 | 0.25 | 4 | 1 |
| financeWork | – | – | 0.7 | 0.3 | 2 | 0.5 |

Proposed definition of `financeWork`: "Finance and accounting tasks a developer does or automates alongside coding: building and auditing spreadsheets, reconciling and aggregating figures from exports, invoices and reports, budget and valuation models, and multi-step workflows across business apps. A wrong number costs more than a slow answer."

The rates follow from that last sentence: cost matters moderately (2 points per doubling), time barely (0.5).

## What the simulation showed

- **Coverage holds.** Every candidate that has an Intelligence Index also has the other three, so nothing drops out: 162 candidate rows across 69 provider models.
- **`financeWork` produces different picks.** On OpenCode Go, Kimi K3.1 Pro overtakes Gemini 4 Argon, and Grok 4.7 (Xhigh) enters the top three with intelligence 35.5 but Finance 51.7.
- **Coding picks barely move.** Engineering tracks intelligence so closely that agenticCoding and codeReview keep the same models; the main change is the recommended effort level.
- **The indexes are not on the same scale.** Strategy & Ops runs high for cheap models: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 scores 32.6 on intelligence and 49.2 on Strategy & Ops. A 0.4 weight in softwareFactory therefore lifts cheap models further; I cannot tell from the data whether that is real tool-use skill or how the index is built.

Top pick per provider (OpenCode Zen matches Copilot):

| Category | Copilot | OpenCode Go | ClinePass |
|---|---|---|---|
| agenticCoding | Gemini 4 Carbon (High) | Gemini 4 Argon (High) | Kimi K3.1 Pro |
| codeReview | Gemini 4 Carbon (High) | Gemini 4 Argon (High) | Kimi K3.1 Pro |
| softwareFactory | GPT-6.1 Sol (Medium) | Claude Haiku 5.5 (High) | DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 (High) |
| llmWiki | GPT-6.1 Sol (Medium) | Claude Haiku 5.5 (Xhigh) | DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 (Max) |
| financeWork | Gemini 4 Carbon (High) | Kimi K3.1 Pro | Kimi K3.1 Pro |

## Round 4

❓ **Q17 - The blends and the definition**: Should the config use the quality mixes, rates and `financeWork` description above, with `financeWork` as the fifth category instead of `dataAggregation`?

➡️ Yes as a starting point. The coding mixes are nearly cosmetic, but they state the intent and will matter if Engineering ever diverges from intelligence.

---

❓ **Q18 - Raw index points**: Should the indexes be mixed as raw points, with no rescaling to a common range? Rescaling would correct the Strategy & Ops scale difference, but it brings back the dependence on the candidate pool that Q6 removed.

➡️ Yes, raw points, with the scale difference recorded in the config notes and the softwareFactory Strategy & Ops weight kept at 0.4 or lower.

---

❓ **Q19 - Show quality on the site**: Should the site show the blended quality for the category in place of the plain intelligence column from Q12, next to effort, $ per task and response time?

➡️ Yes. Quality minus the two penalties then adds up to the score a reader sees.
Q19: Wait with that. I'll redesign later. Rest recommended, additionally I think we can agenticCoding /softwareFactory names into something like coding heavy / coding light. I'm open to proposals.

Deferring the site redesign is fine, but the live site reads the scoring output directly, so the new scoring changes what it displays whether or not anyone touches it. That adds one question to this round.

## What the current site depends on

[site/index.html](site/index.html) is published daily together with `config/categories.json` and `recommendations.json`. With the new scoring and no site change:

- **The "Tok/s" column** would show a response time in seconds, or a dash, depending on the output field name.
- **The weights list** under each category would be empty, because it reads `weights` from the config.
- **The score** would print with three decimals on a roughly 30–60 scale.
- **The footer** would still describe min-max normalization and the per-category token ratio, both removed.
- **The model name** would not show the recommended effort unless it is part of the name string.

## Round 5

❓ **Q20 - Category names**: Should `agenticCoding` become `codingHeavy` and `softwareFactory` become `codingLight`, with the other three names unchanged?

- `codingHeavy`: "Open-ended coding left running for hours with little supervision, where a wrong turn is expensive: planning, debugging, large refactors."
- `codingLight`: "Well-scoped, already-planned coding tasks done in volume, where throughput and cost matter more than peak capability."

Alternatives I considered: `codingHard` / `codingRoutine`, which describe the task rather than the load, and `codingAutonomous` / `codingScoped`, which are closer to the current descriptions but longer.

➡️ Yes, `codingHeavy` and `codingLight`. They read as a pair, and the site's title-casing renders them as "Coding heavy" and "Coding light".

---

❓ **Q21 - Minimal site patch now**: Should the scoring change include a small truthfulness patch to the site, with no layout or styling changes: effort in the model name, column headers matching the new fields, the rates shown in place of the weights list, and a corrected footer? The alternatives are holding the scoring change on a branch until your redesign, or shipping it and letting the site be wrong in the meantime.

➡️ Yes. It is about 20 lines, and it keeps the public page accurate without pre-empting the redesign.

---

❓ **Q22 - Shared understanding**: Is this the full design, and should I implement it once Q20 and Q21 are answered?

- **Candidates:** every AA effort variant of each mapped model, priced at the provider's cheapest row; one row per model at its best-scoring effort; top 2 per provider.
- **Score:** quality − *a* × log2(cost per task) − *b* × log2(response time ÷ 60 s), with cost floored at $0.25 and time at 15 s.
- **Quality:** a per-category mix of the Intelligence, Engineering, Finance & Accounting and Strategy & Ops indexes in raw points, weights summing to 1.
- **Cost per task:** unchanged, with a fixed 3:1 blend; `outputToInputRatio` removed.
- **Response time:** time to first answer token + 500 ÷ tokens per second, from `performance_v3` only.
- **Categories:** `codingHeavy`, `codingLight`, `codeReview`, `llmWiki`, `financeWork`, with the mixes and rates from round 4.
- **Unchanged:** the mapping file, the blacklist, the index-version check, and skipping any model that lacks an input.
- **Left out:** plan caps, cache prices, copywriting and design categories, Pro-tier fields.

Details I would settle myself unless you object: only AA's known effort labels count as variants (so a dated release is not mistaken for one), and a label like "Max, Default Fallback" is shown as "Max".

➡️ Yes.

The agreed design is implemented and scores today's cached data: 69 models across 162 effort variants, in five categories. Typecheck, lint and format are clean, and the patched site renders the new output with no console errors. I did not run the full `npm start`, because this checkout has no `AA_API_KEY`; I ran the scoring step alone on a copy of the main checkout's `data/`.

## What changed

- **[config/categories.json](config/categories.json):** the five categories (`codingHeavy`, `codingLight`, `codeReview`, `llmWiki`, `financeWork`), each with a quality mix, two exchange rates, and a description that says which score components matter. The two floors ($0.25 per task, 15 s) are top-level settings, and the notes explain the formula and its known simplifications.
- **[src/scoring/compute-scores.ts](src/scoring/compute-scores.ts):** scores every effort variant of each mapped model, lists each model once at its best effort, and reads response time from `performance_v3` only. It refuses to run if a quality mix does not sum to 1 or names an unknown index.
- **[site/index.html](site/index.html):** labels only. Effort appears after the model name, the columns are Score, Quality, $/task, Time and $/1M, the rates replace the old weights list, and the footer describes the new formula.

## Top pick per provider

| Category | Copilot | OpenCode Go | ClinePass |
|---|---|---|---|
| Coding heavy | Gemini 4 Carbon (Medium) | Gemini 4 Argon (High) | Kimi K3.1 Pro |
| Coding light | GPT-6.1 Sol (Medium) | Claude Haiku 5.5 (High) | DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 (High) |
| Code review | Gemini 4 Carbon (High) | Gemini 4 Argon (High) | Kimi K3.1 Pro |
| LLM wiki | GPT-6.1 Sol (Medium) | Claude Haiku 5.5 (Xhigh) | DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 (Max) |
| Finance work | Gemini 4 Carbon (High) | Kimi K3.1 Pro | Kimi K3.1 Pro |

OpenCode Zen's top pick matches Copilot's in every category.

## Things to know

- **Output shape changed.** Each row in `recommendations.json` now has `effort`, and `breakdown` holds `quality`, `costPerTask`, `responseTimeSeconds` and the four indexes; `breakdown.speed` is gone. The category keys changed too, so history snapshots on the `data` branch will not line up with new ones.
- **Ties go to the cheaper variant.** Two efforts of one model can land on the same rounded score (Gemini 4 Carbon at Medium and High both score 59.2 for coding heavy), so I added that rule; it was not part of what we agreed.
- **Leftover files.** The worktree now has a `data/` copy of the cached inputs (gitignored).
